items.title: Activation of Amino Acids and the Phases of Translation

source_refs.note: Activation of amino acids and the three phases of translation (PDF 137-140); Figures 19.17 to 19.20 are replaced by original diagrams.

blocks.text: Before protein synthesis the building units are prepared: specific tRNAs attach to specific amino acids to make aminoacyl-tRNAs (aa-tRNA). The enzyme aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase does this; there are 20 kinds, each binding one amino acid and recognising the tRNAs with anticodons for it. The aa-tRNA delivers the amino acid to the ribosome.

blocks.alt: An amino acid plus ATP plus a matching tRNA, drawn as a box with its anticodon at the bottom, react on an enzyme labelled aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase to give an aminoacyl-tRNA, the same tRNA with the amino acid attached at its top.
blocks.caption: Making an aminoacyl-tRNA (original diagram after Figure 19.17).
blocks.long_description: Before protein synthesis each amino acid is joined to its own tRNA, making an aminoacyl-tRNA (aa-tRNA). The enzyme aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase does this; there are 20 kinds, one for each amino acid, and each recognises its amino acid and the tRNAs with anticodons for that amino acid. The aa-tRNA delivers its amino acid to the ribosome, where its anticodon pairs with a codon of the mRNA.

items: The aa-tRNA carrying the first amino acid binds the small ribosomal subunit, a step controlled by an initiation factor. In prokaryotes the first amino acid is N-formyl-methionine; in eukaryotes it is unmodified methionine.
Another initiation factor attaches the 5' end of the mRNA to the small subunit, placing the anticodon of the aa-tRNA over the first codon, AUG.
The large subunit joins. The initiation complex now has both subunits, the first aa-tRNA, the mRNA and the factors.

blocks.caption: Sites on the ribosome
rows: where the first aa-tRNA sits and peptide bonds form

blocks.text: Along the mRNA the sites lie in the order E-P-A from 5' to 3', because the ribosome moves towards the 3' end.

blocks.alt: Three panels with a ribosome over a red mRNA reading AUG, UUU, GGC, UAA, the large subunit marked E, P and A. Initiation: a tRNA with anticodon UAC carrying Met sits at P on AUG. Elongation: Met-tRNA at P and Phe-tRNA (AAA) at A with a peptide bond forming. Termination: tRNA at P holds the chain while a release factor sits at the stop codon UAA in the A site and the polypeptide is released.
blocks.caption: Initiation, elongation and termination (original diagram after Figures 19.18 to 19.20).
blocks.long_description: Initiation: the aa-tRNA carrying the first amino acid (N-formyl-methionine in prokaryotes, methionine in eukaryotes) binds the small ribosomal subunit with an initiation factor, the 5' end of the mRNA is attached so its anticodon lies over the start codon AUG, and the large subunit joins. The ribosome has a P site, an A site and an E site, ordered E-P-A from 5' to 3'. Elongation: an aa-tRNA with the matching anticodon enters the A site with an elongation factor; peptidyl transferase joins the chain on the P-site tRNA to the new amino acid by a peptide bond; the ribosome moves three nucleotides towards the 3' end (translocation), shifting the chain to P and the empty tRNA to E. Termination: at a stop codon no tRNA fits; a release factor frees the polypeptide and the subunits separate.

items: The next aa-tRNA, with the matching anticodon and amino acid, binds the A site with the help of an elongation factor.
Peptidyl transferase removes the amino acid (first, methionine) from the tRNA at the P site and joins it by a peptide bond to the amino acid of the tRNA at the A site.
The ribosome moves three nucleotides along the mRNA in the 5' to 3' direction (translocation).
The tRNA carrying the chain shifts from the A site to the P site, a new codon is exposed at A, and the empty tRNA moves to E and leaves.
These steps repeat until a stop codon reaches the A site.

blocks.text: When a stop codon is at the A site no aa-tRNA comes, because no tRNA has an anticodon for a stop codon. A protein called a release factor recognises the stop codon and releases the polypeptide from the tRNA at the P site; the tRNA is released and the ribosomal subunits separate from the mRNA.
